judged_text: In updateEvent the fallback `event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId` is only reached when externalCalendarId is falsy, so it compares cal.externalId against undefined and never matches, yielding selectedCalendar === undefined. Any updateEvent call without externalCalendarId (e.g. EventManager passing calenderExternalId=null for legacy references) now calls calendar.events.update with calendarId undefined — the event update fails against the wrong/undefined calendar, where the old code fell back to destinationCalendar.externalId; the dead find() was clearly meant to use mainHostDestinationCalendar.

adjudication.rationale: In `packages/app-store/googlecalendar/lib/CalendarService.ts` `updateEvent`, `selectedCalendar` is now computed as `externalCalendarId ? externalCalendarId : event.destinationCalendar?.find((cal) => cal.externalId === externalCalendarId)?.externalId;`. When `externalCalendarId` is falsy (the only time the fallback runs), the predicate compares `cal.externalId` to `externalCalendarId` (i.e., `null`/`undefined`), so it will not match any real calendar externalId and yields `undefined`. This removes the previous fallback behavior (`event.destinationCalendar?.externalId`) and can cause updates (and similarly the `calendarId` computed in `deleteEvent`) to target the wrong calendar (likely falling back elsewhere to `primary`) or fail, especially when callers pass `null` (e.g., `EventManager.updateCalendarEvents` sets `calenderExternalId` to `null` when no `externalCalendarId` exists).
